pr_title: add randomness to nodeStatusReportFrequency for kubelet
pr_body:
Adding one time [-50% , +50%] randomness to `nodeStatusReportFrequency` after initial node status update.
It helps spread the load from kubelet evenly

@SergeyKanzhelev was reflecting the request from the person working on the issue - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/124202#issuecomment-2442663774

>Would it be better to just add some random delay in the beginning once node is registered successfully the first time, instead of changing the reporting interval?

A cross-cutting failure can possibly cause all nodes to become NotReady. When the failure is resolved, all kubelet changed status to be Ready at the same time and then all future node status update will become mostly synchronized again.  e.g. a VPC service outage or a user misconfiguration may cause CNI to make the node NotReady. When the issue is fixed, kubelet status report time are synchronized again which is undesired.

The idea is similar to how we add jitter to `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency`.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/66b3dc1a389d24620fc92ddfaca5f35190ef660d/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1684
we had several problems recently adjusting node reporting timeouts and some controllers setting the node unready or with some side effects so this should be carefully reviewed
@aojea Can you please link the GH issues regarding the issue that you mentioned above?

I also vaguely remember something along these lines. Maybe https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/127352 triggered me.

But the point is - there may be some expectations on how fast node will reconcile status, so changing it even 25% may affect things negatively.

Adding a small jitter after `changed` triggered the update and keep subsequent updates in standard configured intervals may be a better approach to keep the predictability of node status update behavior.

Thanks for the pointer to the issue! This issue seems to be about nodeStatus**Update**Frequency but not nodeStatus**Report**Frequency.

From my understanding, there are 2 things in kubelet:
- nodeStatus**Update**Frequency: frequency to ~~update lease object~~ calculate node status for the node. It has 10-second by default. If the lease not updated within `node-monitor-grace-period`, it will be set as NotReady by the node controller in kube-controller-manager.
- nodeStatus**Report**Frequency: frequency to update node/status subresource. It has 5-minute by default when there's no status change. Please note that kubelet will **immediate** update the node/status when there's a status change.

Given the kubelet **won't** wait for `nodeStatusReportFrequency` when there's a status change. IMO it should not be a problem if we make it to be 75% - 125% of the specified `nodeStatusReportFrequency`.

If you think this is still a strong concern, I'm happy to change it to be 75% - 100% of the specified `nodeStatusReportFrequency` or something like 80% - 100%.

Please let me know WDYT?

**EDIT**: `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` doesn't control lease renew frequency.
Lease renew frequency is controlled by `leaseDuration` multiply a fixed `nodeLeaseRenewIntervalFraction` which is 0.25 now.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c56aa5a58904ec9910b6bf29385a8b85fb115be/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L920

Yes, I realize it is not the issue directly affecting this one. Have you looked into any logic k8s owns that may depend on this interval?

Do you think the proposal of a single jitter after a forced update works? Or you want to randomize the interval?

>Yes, I realize it is not the issue directly affecting this one. Have you looked into any logic k8s owns that may depend on this interval?

I haven't found anything depends on `nodeStatusReportFrequency `. I have tested with 30m with [-25%, 25%] jitter in a larger than 5k-node cluster setup. It seems to be working fine.

>Do you think the proposal of a single jitter after a forced update works? Or you want to randomize the interval?

To prevents kubelet status update from becoming synchronized again due to some crosscutting event as I described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128394#issuecomment-2443363423, IMO it's more robust to always randomize the interval.

> To prevents kubelet status update from becoming synchronized again due to some crosscutting event as I described in [#128394 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128394#issuecomment-2443363423), IMO it's more robust to always randomize the interval.

I don't understand what do you mean by more robust, if any node starts in a random interval and the frequency is fixed , the randomness of the beginning is maintained,  the other approach is completely random and more unpredictable for debugging .... having deterministic patterns always help to troubleshoot problems because the outliers help to identify the issues

I'm still confused with the fields and the relations


https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d353417cd38d8f4980ff1bff71362895402a8ba/cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/options/nodelifecyclecontroller.go#L41-L45

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d353417cd38d8f4980ff1bff71362895402a8ba/pkg/kubelet/apis/config/v1beta1/defaults.go#L119-L127

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d353417cd38d8f4980ff1bff71362895402a8ba/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L270-L291

I don't see this as clear as it seems, someone that sets the NodeStatusUpdateFrequency explicitly will use that value for NodeStatusReportFrequency ... there is a lot of rabbit holes here 😄 

Sergey suggestion is more conservative and should solve the problem

```
diff --git a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go b/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go
index 5c07e4367af..4ea871dc259 100644
--- a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go
+++ b/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go
@@ -1681,7 +1681,7 @@ func (kl *Kubelet) Run(updates <-chan kubetypes.PodUpdate) {
                        // Call updateRuntimeUp once before syncNodeStatus to make sure kubelet had already checked runtime state
                        // otherwise when restart kubelet, syncNodeStatus will report node notReady in first report period
                        kl.updateRuntimeUp()
-                       wait.JitterUntil(kl.syncNodeStatus, kl.nodeStatusUpdateFrequency, 0.04, true, wait.NeverStop)
+                       wait.JitterUntil(kl.syncNodeStatus, kl.nodeStatusUpdateFrequency, 0.25, true, wait.NeverStop)
                }()
 
                go kl.fastStatusUpdateOnce()
```

everytime we change some parameter or behavior that seems not important it always bit us, especially those related to node status

Sorry about the delayed response.

The relationship between them is:
 Kubelet uses 0.25 * `NodeLeaseDurationSeconds` as the renew interval. Currently the renew interval is 10s.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6cb5ea56cb96f6a4ddec677d3d94faf07179368d/staging/src/k8s.io/kubelet/config/v1beta1/types.go#L284-L293

The node status will be set to `NotReady` if kubelet failed to renew its lease within `nodeMonitorGracePeriod`
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6cb5ea56cb96f6a4ddec677d3d94faf07179368d/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L270-L291

The `NodeStatusUpdateFrequency` is how frequently kubelet compute the node status. Kubelet only updates node status in APIServer in one of the following condition 1) there's a status change 2) lastStatusUpdateTime + `NodeStatusReportFrequency` < currentTime. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6cb5ea56cb96f6a4ddec677d3d94faf07179368d/pkg/kubelet/apis/config/types.go#L188-L192

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6cb5ea56cb96f6a4ddec677d3d94faf07179368d/pkg/kubelet/apis/config/types.go#L193-L197

Given 1) `nodeMonitorGracePeriod` doesn't depend on `NodeStatusReportFrequency` 2) when there's a node status change, the worst latency for kubelet to reflect it in nodeStatus is `NodeStatusUpdateFrequency` but not `NodeStatusReportFrequency` 3) this PR doesn't touch `NodeStatusUpdateFrequency`, the risk of this PR should low.

issue_context.title: kubelet periodic node status update should not be aligned
issue_context.body:
### What happened? The default `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` is 10s with 4% jitter. The default `nodeStatusReportFrequency` is 5m. The node status will be updated either there's a change or it has been longer than `nodeStatusReportFrequency` since the previous update. `nodeStatusReportFrequency` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/55b83c92b3b69cd53d5bf22b8ccff859a005241a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L580-L581 The jitter of `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` won't effectively make the periodic node status update to be spread evenly over the 5-minute window. The node status update requests from thousands of nodes are still sent at almost the same time after a couple of days. It can cause the CPU usage to spike every 5 minutes. The following is the APIServer CPU utilization on 96CPU instances. The cluster has 5k nodes that are added in a short period of time. The cluster is idle without any application workload. The utilization can go up to 64% and go down to 14% just because of these node status update requests. ### What did you expect to happen? I'd expect the node status update requests from kubelet to be spread evenly so that the apiserver won't have a minute that it has to handle the requests from most nodes every 5 minutes. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? Bring up a cluster and add nodes in a short period of time. ### Anything else we need to know? Ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105272/files _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
Cutting edge 1.30 ```console $ kubectl version # paste output here ```
